transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-04-22    Start: 15:30 PDT    Duration: 46 min    Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE); Marco Diaz (Redwood SE); Priya Raman (Novara VP Product); Ethan Cole (Novara Lead ML Eng); Jordan Wu (Novara Security Arch)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, access gaps, and a surprising performance discrepancy between the pilot bench results and Novara's staging traffic. Action items assigned around re-running benches with KV/prefix cache enabled, providing payload traces, and clarifying KMS/SSO constraints.

Topics: onboarding checkpoints; staging vs pilot benchmark variance; KV/prefix cache impact; KMS and SSO integration timing; dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs; next steps and demo schedule.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Sasha Patel: okay hey everyone thanks for making time, uh we'll run about 45 minutes, quick agenda—access updates, bench results walk, identify gaps, and pull together next steps.
00:18 Priya Raman: thanks Sasha yes we only have the core crew here today, want to get this moving along since stakeholders asked for a readout by end of month.
00:30 Marco Diaz: cool, quick status from our side - we've got sandbox creds to the gateway, but the KV cache toggle wasn't enabled on your staging cluster so our continuous batching tests were missing that signal.
00:46 Ethan Cole: yeah that explains a lot. we ran the bench earlier this week and saw tail latency spikes at 95th that didn't match what you showed in the onboarding deck. so maybe cache is the reason.
01:02 Marco Diaz: exactly, when we re-ran locally with small prefix caching we saw 30-40% improvement in token/sec and the 95p came down 180-200ms on our model suite.
01:18 Jordan Wu: quick security question, before you re-run anything, do we need to set up a separate KMS key for pilot data? we have strict residency rules and our compliance team said HSM-backed keys are required for production.
01:33 Sasha Patel: good call Jordan —for pilot we can support customer-managed KMS, and Redwood can accept HSM-backed keys via our Private deployment flow but it will add ~2-3 weeks if you want on-prem HSM integration. for the hosted pilot we can use a scoped CMK in provider KMS as a stopgap, but we'll log that in the security doc.
01:53 Jordan Wu: ok please add that to action items, and also need the SOC2 scope doc.
02:02 Sasha Patel: yes I'll share the SOC2 attestation and the current cert matrix after the call.
02:08 Priya Raman: re: the bench numbers — one weird thing: Novara's staging traffic includes a high proportion of short-prompts (single-question queries) that amplifies opening-token overhead. did you simulate that distribution in your tests?
02:25 Marco Diaz: we used a mixed distribution but I think our default bench had slightly longer average sequence lengths. if you can upload a small trace of anonymized payloads that will let us mirror it exactly.
02:36 Ethan Cole: we can produce that, but it might take a couple days to scrub PII. we'll get a redacted sample by next week.
02:45 Marco Diaz: perfect, that will allow us to tune batching windows and quant profiles to the real workload.
02:52 Sasha Patel: also wanted to flag cost tradeoffs—short prompts make batching less effective, so caching/prefix reuse matters more. dedicated capacity helps consistency but costs more; we'll put numbers in the pricing sheet.
03:08 Priya Raman: product is sensitive to tail latency above 350ms, especially in the clinician workflow. can you confirm the 95p target under the dedicated capacity plan?
03:20 Marco Diaz: with dedicated and KV/prefix cache we can hit ~250-300ms 95p depending on model and sequence length. without cache it trends higher. we need the payload trace to estimate precisely.
03:34 Ethan Cole: another anomaly we saw: the bench showed lower throughput at our longer sequences than expected, maybe quantization profile mismatch? we used q4_0 on our end.
03:47 Marco Diaz: yeah q4_0 is conservative but can cause some perf regressions on longer seqs; switching to q4_k_m or q5b for those routes sometimes helps, at the expense of model quality slightly. we'll run a quick sweep.
04:00 Sasha Patel: Marco can you do two runs: (A) match Novara's sequence distribution and cache on, (B) same distribution cache off, and include q4_0 vs q4_k_m comparisons? add p95/p99 and mean tokens/sec.
04:16 Marco Diaz: yep I'll schedule those and post the sheet. estimating 24–48 hours to complete given current queue.
04:25 Priya Raman: timeline wise, we want a bench that mirrors production by next Thursday so execs can sign off on pilot extension.
04:33 Sasha Patel: understood, we'll prioritize.
04:37 Jordan Wu: I had a note on SSO —Novara needs SAML and SCIM; what's Redwood's timeline for SCIM provisioning in Private vs Hosted?
04:48 Marco Diaz: Hosted supports SAML now; SCIM is available in Dedicated and Private today for provisioning, and Hosted SCIM is on our roadmap Q2 but not yet GA. for pilot you can use manual provisioning or Dedicated if you want full SCIM.
05:03 Jordan Wu: manual works for now but we need an enterprise-grade flow before GA.
05:09 Priya Raman: one more thing on observability — we saw token-level cost estimates that didn't match our internal cost model. can you explain the assumptions in your cost calc?
05:20 Sasha Patel: sure we base hosted per-token on average model tokenization and include runtime amortized infra. we'll send a breakdown with per-token and per-route examples; if you share route volumes we can generate an expected monthly number.
05:36 Ethan Cole: also the bench spreadsheet you shared earlier had the 'context reset' column blank—are you doing KV cache prefix reuse across requests or resetting KV each request?
05:48 Marco Diaz: by default tests reset KV, but our continuous bench has a prefix reuse mode which better simulates session-based reuse. that's probably why your numbers diverged.
05:58 Ethan Cole: ah that explains it—our staging traffic is sessiony so lots of reuse.
06:05 Marco Diaz: okay, we'll re-run with prefix reuse and report both metrics.
06:11 Sasha Patel: switching gears—on credentials we need read-only IAM roles for the gateway and temporary service accounts. Ethan, can you share who on infra can create those? also include any IP allowlist ranges.
06:24 Ethan Cole: I'll ping infra, it's Kevin, and he'll create the roles. I'll send the contact and the allowlist ranges today.
06:31 Priya Raman: on the pilot success criteria: we defined three things—95p latency <350ms, model accuracy within 2% of current baseline, and cost per 1k requests below $X. are we aligned?
06:45 Sasha Patel: yes, those look good. we'll add the exact current baseline numbers once we see your sample payloads.
06:52 Jordan Wu: regarding KMS—if we do customer-managed keys in hosted, how do you handle key rotation and attestations? we need proof for audit.
07:03 Sasha Patel: we support CMK rotation lifecycle hooks and will provide rotation logs; for audit we can give KMS access logs and Novak—sorry Novara—can request periodic attestation exports. for HSM-backed on-prem we can do more strict control but requires additional integration time.
07:24 Priya Raman: slight transcription glitch—sorry—question on throttling: what happens if we exceed reserved throughput on Dedicated? does Redwood provide fallback or auto-scale?
07:37 Marco Diaz: Dedicated supports configured autoscaling policies and burst capacity. we can set automatic fallback to compatible model variants in Hosted pool if you use hybrid routing; we'll document the latency tradeoffs.
07:50 Ethan Cole: do you have a playbook for circuit breaker behavior? we need deterministic failure modes for the clinician flow.
08:00 Marco Diaz: yes we have a fallback policy with circuit breakers and can set hard/soft SLOs per route. we'll share the playbook link.
08:10 Sasha Patel: ok real quick recap and owners: Marco runs benches with prefix reuse + quant sweeps; Sasha shares SOC2/KMS docs and pricing delta; Ethan provides traces and infra contact; Jordan confirms KMS constraints. any other items?
08:27 Priya Raman: please add the timeline for the dedicated capacity quote, we need that for budget planning.
08:34 Sasha Patel: will include in the pricing doc, ETA 2026-04-25 for quote.
08:38 Jordan Wu: small nit—can you put the security artifacts in the secure share rather than email? we need control over access.
08:45 Sasha Patel: absolutely, I'll add them to the shared s3 with restricted access and send links.
08:51 Ethan Cole: thanks folks this was helpful, we'll get the trace and infra contact. aim to reconvene after bench rerun.
08:58 Sasha Patel: great, let's tentatively schedule a 30-min follow-up for 2026-04-27 to go over the new numbers.
09:06 Priya Raman: works for us.

--- End Transcript ---

Recap / Next Steps (verbatim):
- Marco: rerun p95/p99 with KV/prefix reuse and q4_0 vs q4_k_m, post by 2026-04-24
- Sasha: share SOC2 attestation, cert matrix, and pricing delta by 2026-04-23/25
- Ethan: deliver redacted sample payloads and infra contact (Kevin) by 2026-04-30
- Jordan: confirm KMS/HSM constraints and preferred provisioning contact by 2026-04-23
